questions.q: What does GitHub add on top of plain Git?
options: GitHub replaces Git entirely with a different system
Nothing — GitHub and Git are the exact same product
Hosting for Git repositories, plus collaboration tools like pull requests, code review, issues, and project boards
GitHub is only a text editor for writing code
questions.explain: Git is the version control system itself; GitHub hosts repositories and adds a collaboration layer on top.

options: A named reference to a repository hosted elsewhere, used to send and receive commits
A branch that exists only on your local machine
A type of merge conflict
A setting that disables commit history
questions.explain: A remote is simply a bookmarked URL for another copy of the repository that your local repo can sync with.

questions.q: What does `git remote add origin <url>` do?
options: Downloads the entire repository and its history
Deletes the current remote
Immediately pushes all commits to GitHub
Attaches a remote named origin, pointing at that URL, to a repository you already have locally — without transferring anything yet
questions.explain: remote add just records the connection; actually sending commits is a separate step (git push, covered in Lesson 8).

questions.q: How does `git clone <url>` differ from `git remote add` on an existing local repo?
options: They are identical commands with different names
clone downloads an existing repository and its full history, and sets up origin automatically, in one step
clone only works for private repositories
clone deletes the remote repository after copying it
questions.explain: git clone combines downloading the repository with configuring the origin remote, unlike remote add which only connects an already-existing local repo.

questions.q: Where on a GitHub repository page do you find the URL your local Git needs to connect to it?
options: The repository's Settings tab, under Danger Zone
It's emailed to you automatically when the repo is created
There's no way to find this URL — it must be typed from memory
The green "Code" button, which reveals the clone URL (HTTPS, SSH, or GitHub CLI)
questions.explain: The Code button on every repository page exposes the exact URL to use with git remote add or git clone.
